summary: Lust and Stevens compute the Langlands parameters of depth-zero irreducible cuspidal representations π of p-adic classical groups: symplectic, special orthogonal and unitary groups, with p odd. They do it through reducibility points. For each self-dual cuspidal ρ of some GL_n(F), s_π(ρ) is the real s ≥ 0 at which Ind ρ|det|^s ⊗ π reduces. Mœglin's theory turns the reducibility data into the Jordan set Jord(π) and hence the parameter. The main theorem shows three things for depth-zero π. First, Σ⌊s_π(ρ)²⌋ n_ρ ⩾ N_Ĝ, with the depth-zero terms alone summing to N_Ĝ (equality (1.3) where Mœglin's reverse inequality is known). Second, the inertial reducibility data IRed(π) are computed explicitly from the compact-induction data (P, τ). Third, the cuspidals with the same IRed are described and counted, matching one, two or four L-packets. For symplectic groups this describes the cuspidal members of Π_φ ∪ Π_φ′ for any tame parameter φ. The proof goes through several steps. Morris's description of depth-zero cuspidals comes first, then Bushnell–Kutzko covers and Blondel's formula, which turn reducibility points into Hecke-algebra parameters. Those parameters are reduced to the finite reductive quotients and computed with Lusztig's classification (Lusztig series, Jordan decomposition, cuspidal unipotent representations, the SO-to-O extension). A final step counts the L-packet sizes. The atlas plans only the general smooth-representation background (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2–SR.3), Witt theory and local fields; Tau Ceti's general Mackey formula does not cover the Harish-Chandra splitting that (7.5) needs. The other 154 items are missing. The p-adic ones (102) join, as the maintainer asks, the existing Part II of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, SmoothRepresentationsPartII ("types, depth and the construction of supercuspidal representations"), whose id, parent, title and area are kept; that Part II already collects Fintzen, Bushnell–Henniart and Newton–Thorne, which cites this paper. The finite-group computation of §7 and its inputs (52 items) join ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups, the atlas's single owner of Deligne–Lusztig theory. The briefs import GL_m local Langlands from ET.6 and Arthur–Mœglin packets as statements from ML.4. The review collated the extraction with the version of record (Proc. LMS 2020, read from the UEA repository): print corrects seven of the recorded slips and part of an eighth, and introduces two new ones. Of the 38 recorded mistakes, 28 are new and unchanged in print.

items.name: Reducibility point s_π(ρ) (introduction)
items.statement: Let 𝒜^σ(F) be the set of equivalence classes of self-dual irreducible cuspidal representations of some GL_n(F). For π an irreducible cuspidal representation of G and ρ ∈ 𝒜^σ(F) there is at most one real number s = s_π(ρ) ⩾ 0 such that the normalized parabolically induced representation Ind ρ|det(·)|_F^s ⊗ π is reducible (|·|_F the normalized absolute value on F); when there is no such real number (which can happen only for even-dimensional special orthogonal groups and ρ a quadratic character of GL_1(F)) one sets s_π(ρ) = 0.
items.note: Introductory form of the map s_π formalized in §4 (Theorem 4.1 + Remark 4.2); the 'at most one' is Silberger's theorem (s1/s4 items). Needs normalized parabolic induction (SR.2) and cuspidality (SR.3), neither built; the self-duality notion is defined in §3.

items.name: Reducibility set Red(π)
items.statement: For an irreducible cuspidal representation π of G, Red(π) = {(ρ, m) : ρ ∈ 𝒜^σ(F), m ∈ N with 2s_π(ρ) = m + 1}.
items.note: Combinatorial set built from s_π; nothing in the atlas defines it. The central invariant of the paper.

items.name: Mœglin: Jordan set of a cuspidal representation (1.1)
items.statement: (Mœglin [38]) For π an irreducible cuspidal representation of G, the Jordan set is Jord(π) = {(ρ, m) : ρ ∈ 𝒜^σ(F), m ∈ N with 2s_π(ρ) − (m + 1) ∈ 2Z_{⩾0}} = {(ρ, m) : (ρ, m_ρ) ∈ Red(π) and m_ρ − m ∈ 2Z_{⩾0}}, so that Red(π) is the set of maximal elements of Jord(π).
items.note: Cited input (Mœglin, J. Algebra 268 (2003)); Jord is the Mœglin–Tadić Jordan set of [42,37,39]. The atlas mentions 'Moeglin' only for Moeglin–Waldspurger residual spectrum in ET.7a, not Jordan sets. Used to translate (1.2) into (1.3).

items.name: Jordan set predicts the Langlands parameter
items.statement: Expected (and, at least when G is quasi-split, known — see [41]): the Jordan set determines the Langlands parameter φ : 𝒲_F × SL_2(C) → Ĝ ⋊ 𝒲_F whose L-packet Π_φ contains π, by φ = ⊕_{(ρ,m)∈Jord(π)} φ_ρ ⊗ st_m, where φ_ρ is the irreducible representation of 𝒲_F corresponding to ρ under the Langlands correspondence for general linear groups and st_m is the m-dimensional irreducible representation of SL_2(C).
items.note: Motivating input (Mœglin [41], Arthur [2], Mok [43], KMSW [29]); not proved in the paper and not used in the proofs of the main theorem (which is automorphic-side). Weil group: ClassFieldTheory layer 9 / LP0; L-group: RG2.5 'semidirect L-group with its projection'; LLC for GL_n: ET.6. Endoscopic classification of classical groups and L-packets: nowhere in the atlas.

items.name: Dimension identity (1.2)
items.statement: Writing n_ρ for the unique natural number such that ρ is a representation of GL_{n_ρ}(F), one should have Σ_{(ρ,m)∈Jord(π)} m n_ρ = N_Ĝ, where N_Ĝ is the dimension of the natural representation of the complex dual group Ĝ.
items.note: Consequence of the expected parameter formula (dimension count); the paper proves the equivalent (1.3) for depth-zero π (Main Theorem (i)). N_Ĝ: 2N+1 for Sp_{2N}, etc.

items.name: (1.2) is equivalent to (1.3)
items.statement: By (1.1), the equality (1.2) is equivalent to Σ_{ρ∈𝒜^σ(F)} ⌊(s_π(ρ))²⌋ n_ρ = N_Ĝ   (1.3), where ⌊x⌋ denotes the greatest integer not exceeding x; almost all terms in this sum are zero since s_π(ρ) < 1 for all but finitely many ρ ∈ 𝒜^σ(F).
items.note: Elementary: for fixed ρ with s = s_π(ρ) the m with (ρ,m) ∈ Jord(π) are m ≡ 2s−1 mod 2, 1 ⩽ m ⩽ 2s−1, summing to s² (s ∈ Z) or s² − 1/4 = ⌊s²⌋ (s ∈ ½+Z); checked. Finiteness of the support of s_π (≥1 only finitely often) is used but not proved here. Printed text writes 's_ρ(π) < 1' (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E1).

items.name: Self-dual cuspidals of GL_n(F) (symplectic case, p odd)
items.statement: (Blondel [3]) There are self-dual irreducible cuspidal representations of GL_n(F) only for n even or n = 1; for n = 1 these are the pair of unramified characters of order dividing two and the pair of (tamely) ramified quadratic characters.
items.note: Cited input, stated for F = F_o (symplectic case, odd residual characteristic). The depth-zero finite-field analogue (self-dual polynomials exist iff n = 1 or n even, [1]) is in §3. No atlas stage.

items.name: Companion parameter φ′ (symplectic case)
items.statement: Let G be symplectic, so Ĝ is a special orthogonal group with N_Ĝ odd, and let φ be a tame Langlands parameter. Since N_Ĝ is odd, (1.2) implies there is exactly one of the two pairs of quadratic characters (the unramified pair, the ramified pair) for which the multiplicities of the two characters in φ|_{𝒲_F} have the same parity; φ′ is the parameter obtained from φ by exchanging the multiplicities of the two characters in this pair (so φ′ = φ when the multiplicities are equal).
items.note: Parameter-side construction used to state the symplectic Theorem; tame = trivial on wild inertia. No atlas stage for L-parameters of classical groups as representations of 𝒲_F × SL_2(C).

items.name: Symplectic theorem (i): cuspidals in Π_φ ∪ Π_φ′
items.statement: Given a tame Langlands parameter φ for a symplectic group G as above, there is an explicit description of the cuspidal representations in the union of L-packets Π_φ ∪ Π_φ′.
items.locator: §1, Theorem (unnumbered, symplectic case), part (i), p. 3 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Main result, parameter-side reformulation of the general Main Theorem via the local Langlands correspondence for symplectic groups (Arthur). Proved in §§8–9.

items.name: Symplectic theorem (ii): parameter pair of a depth-zero cuspidal
items.statement: Conversely, given a depth-zero cuspidal irreducible representation π of a symplectic group G as above, there is an explicit description of the pair {φ, φ′} of tame Langlands parameters such that π ∈ Π_φ ∪ Π_φ′.
items.locator: §1, Theorem (unnumbered, symplectic case), part (ii), p. 3 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Main result. Remark following: for regular depth-zero cuspidals all multiplicities of characters are ⩽ 1 so φ′ = φ, recovering DeBacker–Reeder [14].

items.name: Regular case recovers DeBacker–Reeder
items.statement: In the situation of regular depth zero irreducible cuspidal representations, the multiplicities of the characters are all at most one, so that φ′ = φ; thus one recovers the description of the representations in an L-packet consisting solely of cuspidal representations from [14].
items.locator: §1, remark after the symplectic Theorem, p. 3 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Comparison with DeBacker–Reeder (Ann. Math. 2009); stated without proof here.

items.name: Self-dual members of an inertial class
items.statement: For ρ ∈ 𝒜^σ(F), denote by [ρ] its inertial equivalence class (the set of unramified twists of ρ). Then [ρ] ∩ 𝒜^σ(F) = {ρ, ρ′} consists of exactly two inequivalent representations, with ρ′ = ρχ for χ an unramified character with ρχ² = ρ; since ρ has depth zero, χ has order 2n_ρ.
items.note: Used throughout: the paper computes only the unordered pair {s_π(ρ), s_π(ρ′)}. Depends on the torsion number of a depth-zero cuspidal of GL_n being n (ρχ ≅ ρ for exactly n unramified χ). §4 gives ρ′ = ρ|det(·)|_F^{πi/(n log q)}.

items.name: Inertial reducibility multiset IRed(π)
items.statement: IRed(π) = {{([ρ], m) : (ρ, m) ∈ Red(π)}}, a multiset.
items.note: The invariant actually computed by the main theorem.

items.name: Parity of m depends only on ρ (depth zero, n_ρ > 1)
items.statement: For ρ ∈ 𝒜^σ(F) of depth zero with n_ρ > 1 and ρ′ its self-dual unramified twist, the exterior square L-function of exactly one of ρ, ρ′ has a pole at s = 0, while for the other it is the symmetric square L-function which has a pole (the same for the Asai and twisted Asai L-functions when F/F_o is quadratic); thus the parity of m such that (ρ, m) ∈ Red(π) should be independent of π and opposite to that for ρ′. Consequently IRed(π) is a set except possibly for the inertial classes of quadratic characters of GL_1(F), and computing IRed(π) determines all elements of Red(π) apart from those attached to characters of GL_1(F) of order at most two.
items.note: Explanatory claim relying on Shahidi's theory ([48]: poles of L-functions ↔ reducibility) and the LLC for GL_n; phrased with 'should' and not proved in the paper. Exterior/symmetric square and Asai L-functions: no atlas stage (AL.2/AL.3 are Godement–Jacquet and Rankin–Selberg only).

items.name: Shahidi: poles of L-functions ↔ reducibility points
items.statement: (Shahidi [48]) Poles of L-functions correspond to reducibility points of parabolic induction.
items.note: Cited input stated only informally (motivation for detecting L-packets by reducibility points; genericity not required by the paper's own method). Langlands–Shahidi method: no atlas stage.

items.name: Main Theorem (i): identity (1.3) for depth zero
items.statement: Let π be a depth zero irreducible cuspidal representation of G. Then Σ_{ρ∈𝒜^σ(F)} ⌊(s_π(ρ))²⌋ n_ρ ⩾ N_Ĝ; more precisely, the sum over depth-zero ρ ∈ 𝒜^σ_[0](F) equals N_Ĝ (8.1). Equality in (1.3) follows where the opposite inequality is known (Mœglin [38], in many cases) or once positive-depth ρ are shown to have s_π(ρ) < 1.
items.note: Main result, as the version of record states it (Introduction, (1.4), p. 1086); arXiv v1 states the equality (1.3) although §8 proves only ⩾ (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E33, corrected in print). Proof in §8 from §5's formula {s_π(ρ), s_π(ρ′)} = {|f_1 ± f_2|/2n} and §7's finite-group computation. G any symplectic, special orthogonal or unitary group, possibly non-quasi-split; p odd. Scope (FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20, RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/5): the local data and the compact-induction description of π used here exclude split SO(1,1) (E7); the paper's §7 likewise excludes SO_2^+ over the finite field, so this case is deferred.

items.name: Main Theorem (ii): IRed(π) is explicitly computable
items.statement: Let π be a depth zero irreducible cuspidal representation of G, where G is not the split two-dimensional special orthogonal group SO(1,1) ≅ GL_1 (E7). The multiset IRed(π) can be computed explicitly from the local data defining π as a compactly induced representation.
items.note: Main result (made precise in §8). Local data: (N_1, N_2) and the cuspidal τ_π = τ_π^(1) ⊗ τ_π^(2) of 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2} with its Lusztig parameters. Scope (FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20, RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/5): the local data and the compact-induction description of π used here exclude split SO(1,1) (E7); the paper's §7 likewise excludes SO_2^+ over the finite field, so this case is deferred.

items.name: Main Theorem (iii): fibres of IRed and their size
items.statement: Let π be a depth zero irreducible cuspidal representation of G, where G is not the split two-dimensional special orthogonal group SO(1,1) ≅ GL_1 (E7). The set of irreducible cuspidal representations π′ of G with IRed(π) = IRed(π′) can be described explicitly in terms of the local data defining π. Moreover, the number of such representations is the expected number in one, two or four L-packets (or, for even special orthogonal groups, half the expected number, as §9.3 and Example 9.6 show; PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E34), this number depending again on the local data.
items.note: Main result; 'expected number in an L-packet' is discussed at the start of §9, with care for even orthogonal groups (Example 9.6). Scope (FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20, RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/5): the local data and the compact-induction description of π used here exclude split SO(1,1) (E7); the paper's §7 likewise excludes SO_2^+ over the finite field, so this case is deferred.

items.name: Proof strategy: covers + Blondel + Morris + Lusztig
items.statement: The reducibility points are computed using Bushnell–Kutzko's theory of covers [12] together with results of Blondel [4], which translate the problem to the computation of parameters in the Hecke algebra of a cover (covers constructed in [36]); the parameters are computed using the explicit description of depth zero irreducible cuspidal representations (§3) together with Lusztig's results on representations of finite reductive groups (§7), taking care that the finite reductive groups need not have connected centre; in particular Proposition 7.9 computes when an irreducible cuspidal representation of an even-dimensional special orthogonal group over a finite field extends to the full orthogonal group.
items.note: Roadmap statement recording the cited inputs; each is itemised in §§3–6 below. Attributes the §3 description to Morris, but §3 cites Moy–Prasad [45] and Vignéras [52] (Morris [Level zero G-types] is not in the bibliography).

items.name: Base fields, residue fields, uniformizer
items.statement: F_o is a locally compact nonarchimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p, and F/F_o an extension of degree at most 2 with Galois generator σ : λ ↦ λ̄. For a field E ⊇ F_o: 𝔬_E its ring of integers, 𝔭_E its maximal ideal, k_E = 𝔬_E/𝔭_E its residue field of cardinality q_E; q = q_F, 𝔬_o = 𝔬_{F_o} etc. A uniformizer ϖ_F of F is fixed with ϖ̄_F = −ϖ_F if F/F_o is quadratic ramified and ϖ̄_F = ϖ_F otherwise; N_{F/F_o} : F^× → F_o^× is the norm map, λ ↦ λλ̄ if [F : F_o] = 2.
items.note: Local-field carrier: Mathlib class IsNonarchimedeanLocalField (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LocalField/Basic.lean:45); LocalFieldsRamification layer 0 plans 'local fields and their finite extensions' (normalized valuation, absolute value ‖x‖_K = q^{−v_K(x)}). The special uniformizer with ϖ̄ = −ϖ (exists as p ≠ 2) is not planned anywhere.

items.name: ε-hermitian space, Witt decomposition and Witt basis
items.statement: Fix ε = ±1 and a nondegenerate F/F_o-ε-hermitian space (V, h) of Witt index N and dimension 2N + N^an: h(λv, μw) = λμ̄ h(v, w) = ελμ̄ \overline{h(w, v)} for v, w ∈ V, λ, μ ∈ F. There is a Witt decomposition V = V^− ⊕ V^an ⊕ V^+ with dim_F V^± = N, dim_F V^an = N^an, h|_{V^±} totally isotropic and h^an = h|_{V^an} anisotropic. H = H^− ⊕ H^+ is the hyperbolic plane with basis e_±, h_H(λ_−e_− + λ_+e_+, μ_−e_− + μ_+e_+) = λ_−μ̄_+ + ελ_+μ̄_−, and h|_{V^−⊕V^+} is isometric to an orthogonal sum of N copies of H. A Witt basis e_1^+, …, e_N^+ of V^+, dual basis e_1^−, …, e_N^− of V^−, and a basis e_1^an, …, e_{N^an}^an of V^an diagonalizing h^an, ordered e_N^−, …, e_1^−, e_1^an, …, e_{N^an}^an, e_1^+, …, e_N^+.
items.note: Witt decomposition is built only for quadratic forms: TauCeti.RegularFormClass.wittDecomposition / wittIndex (TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Witt/Decomposition.lean:238, :221), the QuadraticFormInvariants layer-1 target 'Witt decomposition (Lam I.4.1), the Witt index, the anisotropic part'. Alternating (ε = −1, F = F_o) and hermitian/skew-hermitian forms over a quadratic extension are not covered; GN.2 plans 'quaternionic/hermitian variants'. The status rests on GN.2 for the hermitian and skew-hermitian cases and on QuadraticFormInvariants layer 1 for quadratic forms; a nondegenerate alternating form has N^an = 0.

items.name: Witt tower V_n = V ⊕ nH
items.statement: For n ⩾ 0, V_n = V ⊕ nH with form h_n = h ⊕ h_H ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ h_H (orthogonal), with Witt decomposition V_n = V_n^− ⊕ V^an ⊕ V_n^+, V_n^± = V^± ⊕ nH^±; (V_n : n ⩾ 0) is a Witt tower over V_0 = V. Writing e_{N+i}^± for the image of e_± in the i-th copy of H, V_n has ordered Witt basis e_{N+n}^−, …, e_1^−, e_1^an, …, e_{N^an}^an, e_1^+, …, e_{N+n}^+.
items.note: Orthogonal sum of forms is available for quadratic forms (QuadraticMap.prod); the ε-hermitian tower is not planned.

items.name: Classical groups G_n^+ = U(V_n) and G_n = U(V_n)°
items.statement: G_n^+ = U(V_n) = {g ∈ Aut_F(V_n) : h_n(gv, gw) = h_n(v, w) for all v, w ∈ V_n}, the F_o-points of the reductive group determined by (V_n, h_n) (unitary, symplectic or full orthogonal); G_n = U(V_n)° = {g ∈ G_n^+ : N_{F/F_o} det_F(g) = 1}, the F_o-points of the connected component. G_n = G_n^+ unless G_n^+ is orthogonal (F = F_o, ε = 1), in which case G_n is the special orthogonal group, of index 2. G = G_0, G^+ = G_0^+.
items.note: Mathlib has matrix groups Matrix.symplecticGroup (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SymplecticGroup.lean:101), orthogonal/unitary matrix groups for the standard star, and TauCeti has algebraic-group models TauCeti.Orthogonal / TauCeti.SpecialOrthogonal; no isometry group of a general ε-hermitian form over F/F_o, no non-quasi-split forms. ClassicalGroups layer 0 is over ℂ only. Printed 'for all v, w, ∈ V' (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E2).

items.name: Levi M_n ≅ GL_n(F) × G and parabolic P_n
items.statement: The stabilizer in G_n of the decomposition V_n = nH^− ⊕ V ⊕ nH^+ is a Levi subgroup M_n, standard for the Witt basis, with isomorphism M_n ≃ GL_n(F) × G, g ↦ (g|_{nH^−}, g|_V); the stabilizer of nH^− is a standard parabolic subgroup P_n = M_nN_n with Levi component M_n (block upper triangular; M_n block diagonal).
items.note: Maximal parabolics of classical groups; ReductiveGroups roadmaps plan parabolics abstractly, not this lattice/Witt-basis model.

items.name: Dual lattice and almost self-dual lattices
items.statement: For L an 𝔬_F-lattice in V, the dual lattice is L^# = {v ∈ V : h(v, L) ⊆ 𝔭_F}; L is almost self-dual if L ⊇ L^# ⊇ 𝔭_F L.
items.note: Printed with 'v ∈ L' (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E3). TauCeti has LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodule API (TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean) for bilinear forms over a ring, not for sesquilinear forms with the 𝔭_F-normalization.

items.name: Maximal compacts = stabilizers of almost self-dual lattices
items.statement: Assume G is not the split two-dimensional special orthogonal group SO(1,1) ≅ GL_1. If L is almost self-dual, the stabilizer J = J_L in G of L is a maximal compact subgroup of G, and every maximal compact subgroup arises in this way for a unique almost self-dual lattice L. J^1 denotes the pro-unipotent radical of J: the elements inducing the identity on the k_F-spaces V̄_(1) := L/L^# and V̄_(2) := L^#/𝔭_F L.
items.note: Standard (Bruhat–Tits for classical groups, cf. [44]); stated without proof. RG2.2 plans buildings, 'fixers' and the fixed-point statement for bounded subgroups, with a lattice model only for GL_n; the classical-group lattice model is missing. Uniqueness fails for G = SO(1,1) (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E7). Hypothesis added by FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 (RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/5, E7): for split SO(1,1), L(a, b) = π^a𝔬e_− ⊕ π^b𝔬e_+ with (a, b) = (0, 0) and (0, 1) are both almost self-dual, lie in different orbits and have the same stabilizer 𝔬_F^×, so the lattice is not determined by its stabilizer.

items.name: Residual forms on V̄_(1), V̄_(2)
items.statement: h induces nondegenerate k_F/k_o-forms h_{V̄(1)}(v + L^#, w + L^#) := h(v, w) + 𝔭_F (v, w ∈ L) and h_{V̄(2)}(v′ + 𝔭_F L, w′ + 𝔭_F L) := ϖ_F^{−1} h(v′, w′) + 𝔭_F (v′, w′ ∈ L^#). h_{V̄(1)} is ε-hermitian, while h_{V̄(2)} is (−ε)-hermitian if F/F_o is quadratic ramified and ε-hermitian otherwise (by the choice of uniformizer).
items.note: Reduction of forms; basic to the identification of reductive quotients. Checked: h(L,L) ⊆ 𝔬_F and h(L^#, L^#) ⊆ 𝔭_F follow from 𝔭_F L ⊆ L^#. Printed labels h_V̄, h_V̄# vs h_{V̄(1)}, h_{V̄(2)} are inconsistent.

items.name: Reductive quotient of J_L
items.statement: The induced map J → U(V̄_(1)) × U(V̄_(2)) has kernel J^1, so 𝒢 = 𝒢_L = J/J^1 is naturally a subgroup of the finite reductive group U(V̄_(1)) × U(V̄_(2)); if F = F_o or F/F_o is unramified quadratic, 𝒢 identifies with {(g_1, g_2) ∈ U(V̄_(1)) × U(V̄_(2)) : N_{k_F/k_o}(det_{k_F}(g_1) det_{k_F}(g_2)) = 1}; if F/F_o is ramified quadratic, 𝒢 = U(V̄_(1)) × U(V̄_(2)) with no determinant condition (one factor orthogonal, the other symplectic; E5). In every case 𝒢 has connected component 𝒢° = U(V̄_(1))° × U(V̄_(2))°.
items.locator: §2, p. 6 (arXiv v1); published Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 121 (2020), §2, pp. 1089–1090
items.note: RG2.3 plans the abstract 'connected reductive quotient of the special fiber, pro-unipotent radical and reduction map' for parahoric group schemes, not this concrete identification. The displayed determinant condition is wrong in the ramified unitary case (there 𝒢 is the full U(V̄_(1)) × U(V̄_(2))) (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E5). Statement branched by ramification by FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 (RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/3), applying the confirmed E5: for the ramified unitary line with h(e, e) = 1, J/J^1 = {±1} = O(1), which the determinant condition would exclude.

items.name: J° is parahoric; maximality and index
items.statement: J° = J_L° denotes the inverse image in J of 𝒢°; it is a parahoric subgroup of G and, provided G is not the split two-dimensional special orthogonal group SO(1,1) ≅ GL_1, J is its normalizer in G (for split SO(1,1) the normalizer of 𝔬_F^× is all of F^×, which is not compact; E7). J° is a maximal parahoric subgroup unless one of the factors U(V̄_(i))° is the split SO(1,1,k_F) while G is not itself a two-dimensional special orthogonal group, as listed in s2-maximal-parahoric-exceptions; anisotropic two-dimensional factors SO(2,0,k_F) do not obstruct maximality (E6). Every maximal parahoric subgroup arises in this way. If either F/F_o is quadratic ramified and the orthogonal space among V̄_(1), V̄_(2) is non-zero, or F = F_o, ε = 1 and both V̄_(1), V̄_(2) are non-zero, then J° has index 2 in J; otherwise J = J°.
items.locator: §2, p. 6 (arXiv v1); published Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 121 (2020), §2, pp. 1090–1091
items.note: Parahorics abstractly: RG2.3 ('For a facet construct the smooth affine O_E-group scheme with connected special fiber…'); the lattice description is missing. The maximality criterion as printed conflicts with the refined list on p. 7 (only SO(1,1,k_F) factors obstruct maximality) (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E6). Maximality clause replaced by FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 (RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/4) with the criterion of s2-maximal-parahoric-exceptions, so the two items agree (E6). The normalizer clause now excludes split SO(1,1) (RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/5, E7).

items.name: Parahoric of the anisotropic kernel
items.statement: There is a unique almost self-dual lattice L_an in V^an; G_an = U(V^an)° is compact and normalizes the unique (maximal) parahoric J_an° = J°_{L_an}, with connected reductive quotient 𝒢_an° = U(V̄_(1)^an)° × U(V̄_(2)^an)°, where V̄_(1)^an = L_an/L_an^#, V̄_(2)^an = L_an^#/𝔭_F L_an, N_i^an = dim_{k_F} V̄_(i)^an, N^an = N_1^an + N_2^an. Writing SO(M_1, M_2, k_F) for the special orthogonal group of a form of Witt index M_2 with anisotropic part of dimension M_1 − M_2 ⩽ 2: if F = F_o, ε = −1 then N^an = 0 and 𝒢_an° is trivial; if F = F_o, ε = 1 then 𝒢_an° ≃ SO(N_1^an, 0, k_F) × SO(N_2^an, 0, k_F) with N_i^an ⩽ 2; if F/F_o is unramified quadratic then 𝒢_an° ≃ U(N_1^an, k_F/k_{F_o}) × U(N_2^an, k_F/k_{F_o}) with N_i^an ⩽ 1; if F/F_o is ramified quadratic then 𝒢_an° ≃ SO(N_1^an, 0, k_F) if ε = +1 and SO(N_2^an, 0, k_F) if ε = −1, with N_i^an ⩽ 2 and only one N_i^an non-zero.
items.note: Relies on the classification of anisotropic ε-hermitian forms over local fields (dim ⩽ 4 quadratic, ⩽ 2 hermitian); QuadraticFormInvariants layer 6 plans the quadratic-form classification over local fields, nothing for hermitian forms.

items.name: Standard almost self-dual lattices L_{N_1,N_2}
items.statement: For 0 ⩽ N_1, N_2 with N_1 + N_2 = N, L_{N_1,N_2} := 𝔬_F e_N^− ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝔬_F e_1^− ⊕ L^an ⊕ 𝔬_F e_1^+ ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝔬_F e_{N_1}^+ ⊕ 𝔭_F e_{N_1+1}^+ ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝔭_F e_N^+, with stabilizer J_{N_1,N_2} and parahoric J°_{N_1,N_2}, and 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2} = J°_{N_1,N_2}/J^1_{N_1,N_2}.
items.note: Checked: V̄_(1) contains N_1 hyperbolic planes, V̄_(2) contains N_2.

items.name: Every maximal compact/parahoric is conjugate to a unique standard one
items.statement: Every almost self-dual lattice has the form gL_{N_1,N_2} for some g ∈ G and a unique standard lattice L_{N_1,N_2}; this lattice-orbit statement holds for every G. If moreover G is not the split two-dimensional special orthogonal group SO(1,1) ≅ GL_1, every maximal compact (respectively, maximal parahoric) subgroup is conjugate to a unique standard one J_{N_1,N_2} (respectively, J°_{N_1,N_2}); for split SO(1,1) the labels are not injective on subgroups, since J_{1,0} = J_{0,1} = 𝔬_F^×.
items.note: Stated without proof (Witt's theorem + elementary divisors). Uniqueness of the standard J fails for G = SO(1,1), where J_{1,0} = J_{0,1}. Restricted by FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 (RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/5, E7): the unique standard representative of each lattice orbit is kept for all G; the injectivity of the labels on subgroups is stated only away from split SO(1,1).

items.name: Connected reductive quotients 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2}
items.statement: The choice of Witt basis and the forms on V̄_(1), V̄_(2) give: if F = F_o, ε = −1: 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2} ≃ Sp(2N_1, k_F) × Sp(2N_2, k_F); if F = F_o, ε = 1: 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2} ≃ SO(N_1 + N_1^an, N_1, k_F) × SO(N_2 + N_2^an, N_2, k_F); if F/F_o is quadratic unramified: 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2} ≃ U(2N_1 + N_1^an, k_F/k_o) × U(2N_2 + N_2^an, k_F/k_o); if F/F_o is quadratic ramified: 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2} ≃ SO(N_1 + N_1^an, N_1, k_F) × Sp(2N_2, k_F) if ε = +1 and Sp(2N_1, k_F) × SO(N_2 + N_2^an, N_2, k_F) if ε = −1. Uniformly, writing H̄ for the hyperbolic space over k_F, 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2} ≃ 𝒢^(1)_{N_1} × 𝒢^(2)_{N_2} with 𝒢^(i)_{N_i} = U(N_i H̄ ⊕ V̄_(i)^an)°, i = 1, 2.
items.note: Finite classical groups over k_F: no atlas stage (no finite groups of Lie type roadmap).

items.name: When J°_{N_1,N_2} is not maximal
items.statement: J°_{N_1,N_2} is a maximal parahoric subgroup except where one of the factors 𝒢^(i)_{N_i} is SO(1, 1, k_F) but G is not itself a 2-dimensional special orthogonal group; that is, in the cases: F = F_o, ε = 1, (N, N^an) ≠ (1, 0), with (N_i, N_i^an) = (1, 0) for i = 1 or 2; F/F_o quadratic ramified, N^an = 0 and (ε, N_1) = (1, 1) or (ε, N_2) = (−1, 1).
items.note: Refines the criterion stated on p. 6. This is the maximality criterion; s2-parahoric-Jo-properties now cites it (FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20, RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/4).

items.name: 𝒜_n(F), ρ^σ and self-duality
items.statement: 𝒜_n(F) is the set of equivalence classes of irreducible cuspidal representations of GL_n(F), 𝒜(F) = ⋃_{n⩾1} 𝒜_n(F), n = n_ρ. For ρ ∈ 𝒜_n(F), ρ^σ(g) = ρ(σ(g^{−1})^T) for g ∈ GL_n(F) (σ applied entrywise, T the transpose). ρ is self-dual if ρ^σ ≃ ρ; 𝒜_n^σ(F) and 𝒜^σ(F) = ⋃_{n⩾1} 𝒜_n^σ(F) are the self-dual classes.
items.note: Cuspidality/supercuspidality is planned in SR.3 ('matrix-coefficient criteria for supercuspidality'); σ-self-duality is not. For F = F_o this is ρ^∨ ≃ ρ.

items.name: Depth zero for GL_n
items.statement: ρ ∈ 𝒜(F) is of depth zero if it has nonzero fixed vectors under the pro-unipotent radical of the maximal parahoric subgroup GL_{n_ρ}(𝔬_F) of GL_{n_ρ}(F). 𝒜_[0](F) and 𝒜^σ_[0](F) denote the depth-zero, respectively self-dual depth-zero, classes.
items.note: Moy–Prasad depth in the special case of GL_n; no atlas stage plans depth or Moy–Prasad filtrations. Pro-unipotent radical of GL_n(𝔬_F) = 1 + M_n(𝔭_F) (principal congruence subgroup).

items.name: Depth-zero cuspidals of GL_n(F) are compactly induced
items.statement: Any depth zero ρ ∈ 𝒜_n(F) can be written ρ = c-Ind_{𝐉_ρ}^{GL_n(F)} Λ_ρ, where 𝐉_ρ = F^× GL_n(𝔬_F) is the normalizer of the maximal parahoric J_ρ = GL_n(𝔬_F) and Λ_ρ is an irreducible representation of 𝐉_ρ whose restriction λ_ρ = Λ_ρ|_{J_ρ} is the inflation of an irreducible cuspidal representation τ_ρ of J_ρ/J_ρ^1 ≃ GL_n(k_F). The equivalence class of τ = τ_ρ is uniquely determined by ρ, if ρ is self-dual then τ is self-dual, i.e. τ^σ ≃ τ; conversely, if τ is self-dual then exactly two unramified twists of ρ are self-dual (§4) where τ^σ(g) = τ(σ(g^{−1})^T) for g ∈ GL_n(k_F), σ generating Gal(k_F/k_o).
items.note: Standard (level-zero types; no citation given here). Compact induction is planned in SR.2; the classification is not planned anywhere (ET.6 plans 'the needed supercuspidal/type … theory' for GL_m, in general terms). The paper prints "ρ is self-dual if and only if τ is self-dual", false for GL_1 (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E35); the statement above is the corrected one.

items.name: Green: cuspidal representations of GL_n(k_F)
items.statement: (Green [18]) The equivalence classes of irreducible cuspidal representations τ of GL_n(k_F) are parametrized by regular characters of the multiplicative group of the degree-n extension of k_F, equivalently (after choices) by monic irreducible degree-n polynomials P = P_τ ∈ k_F[X] with P(0) ≠ 0. With σ(P) the polynomial obtained by applying σ to the coefficients, τ^σ corresponds to P^σ(X) := σ(P(0))^{−1} X^{deg(P)} σ(P)(1/X); thus τ is self-dual iff P_τ = P_τ^σ.
items.note: Cited input (Green 1955). Deligne–Lusztig/finite groups of Lie type: no atlas stage; CharacterTheory roadmap covers finite-group character theory only.

items.name: Existence of self-dual irreducible polynomials
items.statement: If k_F = k_o, monic irreducible self-dual polynomials of degree n (with P(0) ≠ 0) exist if and only if n = 1 or n is even (see [1]); if k_F/k_o is quadratic, such polynomials exist if and only if n is odd (see [30, §5.4]).
items.note: Elementary finite-field fact (re-derived in §7.1); formalizable from Mathlib's finite-field Galois theory. Governs which n_ρ occur in 𝒜^σ_[0](F).

items.name: Depth-zero cuspidals of G are compactly induced (Moy–Prasad, Morris)
items.statement: Assume G is not the split two-dimensional special orthogonal group SO(1,1) ≅ GL_1. For π ∈ 𝒜_[0](G) one can write π = c-Ind_{J_π}^G λ_π, where J_π = J_{N_1,N_2} is the (compact open) normalizer of a standard maximal parahoric subgroup J_π° and λ_π is an irreducible representation of J_π whose restriction λ_π° = λ_π|_{J_π°} is a sum of J_π-conjugates of the inflation of an irreducible cuspidal representation τ_π of 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2}.
items.note: Cited input (Moy–Prasad [45], and Morris's level-zero types — the latter not in the bibliography). Fails as stated for G = SO(1,1) ≅ GL_1 (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E7). Compact induction: SR.2; the classification itself is not planned. Hypothesis added by FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 (RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/5, E7). For split SO(1,1) ≅ F^× the depth-zero cuspidals are the characters of F^× trivial on 1 + 𝔭_F; they are not compactly induced from 𝔬_F^× (c-Ind from 𝔬_F^× is infinite-dimensional), and the normalizer of 𝔬_F^× is the noncompact F^×. That case is deferred: it is to be treated separately by characters of F^×, not by compact induction.

items.name: Uniqueness of the parahoric and of τ_π
items.statement: Assume G is not the split two-dimensional special orthogonal group SO(1,1) ≅ GL_1. By [45, 52], the standard maximal parahoric subgroup J_π° is uniquely determined by π, so N_1, N_2 are determined by π, and τ_π is determined up to conjugacy by an element of 𝒢_{N_1,N_2}. Since 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2} = 𝒢^(1)_{N_1} × 𝒢^(2)_{N_2}, τ_π = τ_π^(1) ⊗ τ_π^(2) with τ_π^(i) an irreducible cuspidal representation of 𝒢^(i)_{N_i}.
items.note: Cited input (Moy–Prasad unrefined minimal K-types; Vignéras). Defines the 'local data' of the Main Theorem. Hypothesis added by FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 (RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/5, E7): for split SO(1,1), (N_1, N_2) is not determined by π, since the labels (1, 0) and (0, 1) give the same subgroup.

items.name: Lusztig: cuspidal representations of finite classical groups
items.statement: (Lusztig [32, 33]) The irreducible cuspidal representations τ of 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2} are classified in terms of semisimple elements s of the dual group and unipotent irreducible cuspidal representations of the centralizer of s, generalizing Green's classification. The only unipotent irreducible cuspidal representation of GL_n(k_F) is the trivial representation of GL_1(k_F).
items.note: Cited input, recalled precisely in §7. Deligne–Lusztig theory, Lusztig series and Jordan decomposition: no atlas stage; a Part II (or a finite-groups-of-Lie-type roadmap) would need them.

items.name: Induced representation I(ρ, π, s)
items.statement: For ρ ∈ 𝒜_n(F), π ∈ 𝒜(G) and s ∈ C, I(ρ, π, s) = Ind_{P_n}^{G_n} ρ|det(·)|_F^s ⊗ π, the normalized parabolic induction from P_n = M_nN_n with M_n ≃ GL_n(F) × G, where |·|_F is the normalized absolute value on F (image q^Z) and det is the determinant of GL_n(F).
items.note: SR.2 plans 'normalized induction/Jacquet functors using a specified square root of the modulus character'.

items.name: Unramified twist shifts s
items.statement: I(ρ|det(·)|_F^{s_0}, π, s) = I(ρ, π, s + s_0); thus nothing is lost by replacing ρ by any unramified twist.
items.note: Immediate from the definition once I(ρ,π,s) exists.

items.name: Theorem 4.1(i) (Silberger): reducibility forces a self-dual twist
items.statement: If I(ρ, π, s) is reducible for some s ∈ R, then there exists s_0 ∈ R such that ρ|det(·)|_F^{s_0} is self-dual.
items.note: Cited input: Silberger [49, Corollaries 5.4.2.2–3] (Harish-Chandra's theory of the Plancherel measure / intertwining operators). No atlas stage.

items.name: Theorem 4.1(ii) (Silberger): unique reducibility point
items.statement: If ρ is self-dual and I(ρ, π, s) is reducible for some s ∈ R, then there is a unique real number s_π(ρ) ⩾ 0 such that, for s ∈ R, I(ρ, π, s) is reducible if and only if s = ±s_π(ρ).
items.note: Cited input: Silberger [50, Theorem 1.6]. Defines s_π.

items.name: Remark 4.2: the even-orthogonal exception
items.statement: If ρ is self-dual then I(ρ, π, s) is reducible for some s ∈ R, except: for G an even special orthogonal group, π an irreducible cuspidal representation not normalized by the full orthogonal group G^+, and n = 1 (ρ a trivial or quadratic character of F^×), I(ρ, π, s) is irreducible for all s ∈ R. In this situation π^+ = Ind_G^{G^+} π is an irreducible cuspidal representation of G^+ and I(ρ, π^+, s) is reducible at s = 0.
items.note: Cited input (Jantzen [23]). Explains the convention s_π(ρ) = 0 and the special cases in §§5–6.

items.name: The map s_π : 𝒜^σ(F) → R_{⩾0}
items.statement: For fixed π ∈ 𝒜(G), Theorem 4.1 gives a map s_π : 𝒜^σ(F) → R_{⩾0}, with s_π(ρ) = 0 if I(ρ, π, s) is irreducible for all s ∈ R.
items.note: Formal definition of s_π used in (1.3).

items.name: Basic Assumption: s_π takes values in ½Z (depth zero)
items.statement: Part of the 'Basic Assumption' of Mœglin–Tadić [42] is that the image of s_π lies in ½Z (known in many cases, at least for G quasi-split, by work of Arthur, Mœglin, Waldspurger). The paper proves this independently for depth zero representations π.
items.note: Proved later via §5: s_π values are |f_1 ± f_2|/2n with f_i computed in §7 ('We will see these values are always half-integers').

items.name: The two self-dual unramified twists; depth-zero formula
items.statement: If ρ ∈ 𝒜^σ(F) there are (up to equivalence) exactly two unramified twists of ρ which are self-dual, ρ and ρ′. If moreover ρ has depth zero then ρ′ := ρ|det(·)|_F^{πi/(n log q)}. Hence Silberger's result describes all complex s for which I(ρ, π, s) is reducible; the paper computes only the pair {s_π(ρ), s_π(ρ′)}, which suffices to prove (1.3).
items.note: Depth-zero torsion number n_ρ; consistent with χ of order 2n_ρ in §1.

items.name: Existence of a cover (Miyauchi–Stevens Thm 1.1)
items.statement: Let ρ ∈ 𝒜^σ_[0](F) (a representation of GL_n(F)) and π ∈ 𝒜_[0](G), ρ = c-Ind_{𝐉_ρ}^{GL_n(F)} Λ_ρ, π = c-Ind_{J_π}^G λ_π; put J_M = J_ρ × J_π and λ_M = λ_ρ ⊗ λ_π. By [36, Theorem 1.1] there is a cover (J, λ) of (J_M, λ_M): J is a compact open subgroup of G_n with an Iwahori decomposition with respect to (M_n, P_n) and J ∩ M_n = J_M; λ is an irreducible representation of J with λ|_{J_M} = λ_M and λ|_{J∩N_n^±} a multiple of the trivial representation; the Hecke algebra ℋ(G_n, λ) contains an invertible element supported on the (J, J)-double coset of a strongly positive element of the centre of M_n.
items.note: Cited input (Miyauchi–Stevens, Math. Ann. 358 (2014), semisimple types). Bushnell–Kutzko types/covers: no atlas stage. ℋ(G, λ) (λ-spherical Hecke algebra) is only adjacent to SR.1's 'e_U corners with U-biinvariant Hecke algebras'. Scope (FIX-RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20, RT-PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/5): the local data and the compact-induction description of π used here exclude split SO(1,1) (E7); the paper's §7 likewise excludes SO_2^+ over the finite field, so this case is deferred.

items.name: ℋ(G_n, λ) is a generic Hecke algebra on D_∞ (Miyauchi–Stevens Thm 1.2(i))
items.statement: If there is some g ∈ G_n ∖ M_n normalizing M_n such that the g-conjugate of ρ ⊗ π is equivalent to an unramified twist of ρ ⊗ π, then ℋ(G_n, λ) is a generic Hecke algebra on an infinite dihedral group: it is generated by T_1, T_2, each supported on a single (J, J)-double coset, with relations (T_i − q^{f_i})(T_i + 1) = 0 for some half-integers f_i ⩾ 0; there is a recipe to compute the f_i ([36, §6.3], revisited in §6).
items.note: Cited input [36, Theorem 1.2(i)]. The two parameters f_1, f_2 are the paper's key unknowns.

items.name: Otherwise ℋ(G_n, λ) ≅ C[Z^{±1}] and I(ρ,π,s) is irreducible
items.statement: Otherwise (no such g), ℋ(G_n, λ) is abelian, isomorphic to C[Z^{±1}], and the induced representation I(ρ, π, s) is irreducible for every s ∈ C.
items.note: Cited input [36, Theorem 1.2(ii)] plus the Bushnell–Kutzko comparison.

items.name: The dihedral case always occurs except in the even-orthogonal exception
items.statement: Since ρ is self-dual, the condition in [36, Theorem 1.2(i)] is always satisfied, unless G is an even-dimensional special orthogonal group, π is not normalized by the full orthogonal group G^+, and n = 1.
items.note: Links to Remark 4.2. Stated without proof.

items.name: Subcategories ℜ^{[ρ,π]}(M_n), ℜ^{[ρ,π]}(G_n)
items.statement: ℜ^{[ρ,π]}(M_n) is the full subcategory of smooth complex representations of M_n all of whose irreducible subquotients are unramified twists of ρ ⊗ π; ℜ^{[ρ,π]}(G_n) is the full subcategory of representations of G_n all of whose irreducible subquotients have supercuspidal support an unramified twist of ρ ⊗ π.
items.note: Bernstein blocks: SR.3 plans 'the subquotient description by supercuspidal support. Construct the Bernstein decomposition'.

items.name: Types, covers and the commutative diagram (Bushnell–Kutzko)
items.statement: Since (J, λ) is a cover of (J_M, λ_M), which is a type, there is a normalized embedding of Hecke algebras t : ℋ(M_n, λ_M) ↪ ℋ(G_n, λ) such that the square with horizontal equivalences 𝔥 : ℜ^{[ρ,π]}(G_n) → Mod-ℋ(G_n, λ), 𝔥_M : ℜ^{[ρ,π]}(M_n) → Mod-ℋ(M_n, λ_M) (𝔥_M : ξ ↦ Hom_{J_M}(λ_M, ξ), similarly 𝔥), left vertical Ind_{P_n}^{G_n} and right vertical t_* commutes, where t_* maps a right ℋ(M_n, λ_M)-module X to Hom_{ℋ(M_n,λ_M)}(ℋ(G_n, λ), X), with ℋ(G_n, λ) an ℋ(M_n, λ_M)-module via t.
items.note: Cited input (Bushnell–Kutzko [12], Theorems 4.3/7.9 there). Central to the method; no atlas stage plans types, covers or the Hecke-module equivalence (SR.1 plans only the e_U-corner equivalence for trivial types).

items.name: ℋ(M_n, λ_M) ≅ C[Z^{±1}] and normalization t(Z) = T_2T_1
items.statement: ℋ(M_n, λ_M) ≅ C[Z^{±1}] with Z supported on ζJ_M, where ζ is the element of the centre of M_n acting on V_n = nH^− ⊕ V ⊕ nH^+ as 1 on V and as ϖ_F on nH^+. The element T_2T_1 ∈ ℋ(G_n, λ) is supported on JζJ and, since t(Z) is supported on the same double coset, Z is normalized so that t(Z) = T_2T_1.
items.note: Normalization needed to apply Blondel's formula.

items.name: Blondel: reducibility points from Hecke parameters (5.1)
items.statement: (Blondel [4, Proposition 3.12]) If I(ρ, π, s) is reducible then the real part of s belongs to {±(f_1 ± f_2)/2n}.
items.note: Cited input: computation of simple modules of the rank-one affine Hecke algebra with two parameters, transported by the Bushnell–Kutzko diagram. Sanity check: for G_n = SL_2 = Sp_2 (G trivial, n = 1, ρ = 1) f_1 = f_2 = 1 gives {1, 0}, matching reducibility of the trivial / unramified quadratic principal series.

items.name: {s_π(ρ), s_π(ρ′)} = {|f_1 ± f_2|/2n}
items.statement: The values (f_1 ± f_2)/2n are always half-integers, and {s_π(ρ), s_π(ρ′)} = {|f_1 + f_2|/2n, |f_1 − f_2|/2n}, where ρ′ is the unique self-dual unramified twist of ρ not equivalent to ρ.
items.note: The half-integrality is proved later (§§7–8); the identification uses Theorem 4.1 and §4's description of ρ′.

items.name: 𝒢^{(i)+}_{N_i}
items.statement: 𝒢^{(i)+}_{N_i} denotes the full finite classical group of which 𝒢^(i)_{N_i} = U(N_iH̄ ⊕ V̄^an_(i))° is the connected component; one distinguishes whether τ_π^(i) is normalized by 𝒢^{(i)+}_{N_i}.
items.note: Only differs from 𝒢^(i) for orthogonal factors.

items.name: J° lies in exactly two maximal compacts J_1, J_2
items.statement: The group J in G_n has reductive quotient ≃ GL_n(k_F) × 𝒢_{N_1,N_2}; J° is the inverse image of its connected component. J° is contained in precisely two maximal compact subgroups of G_n: the standard J_2 := J_{N_1,N_2+n} and J_1 conjugate to J_{N_1+n,N_2} (both standard for the reordered Witt basis e_N^−, …, e_{N_1+1}^−, e_{N+n}^−, …, e_{N+1}^−, e_{N_1}^−, …, e_1^−, e_1^an, …, e_{N^an}^an, e_1^+, …, e_{N_1}^+, e_{N+1}^+, …, e_{N+n}^+, e_{N_1+1}^+, …, e_N^+). Their reductive quotients 𝒢_1, 𝒢_2 are ≃ 𝒢_{N_1+n,N_2}, 𝒢_{N_1,N_2+n}, the image of J° in each is a parabolic subgroup with Levi component ≃ GL_n(k_F) × 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2}, and 𝒢_1° ≃ U((N_1+n)H̄ ⊕ V̄^an_(1))° × 𝒢^(2)_{N_2} ⊇ (GL_n(k_F) × 𝒢^(1)_{N_1}) × 𝒢^(2)_{N_2}, 𝒢_2° ≃ 𝒢^(1)_{N_1} × U((N_2+n)H̄ ⊕ V̄^an_(2))° ⊇ 𝒢^(1)_{N_1} × (GL_n(k_F) × 𝒢^(2)_{N_2}).
items.note: From the construction of the cover in [36]; building-theoretic (J° fixes an edge). RG2.2/RG2.3 plan facets and parahorics abstractly.

items.name: Weyl group elements s_1, s_2
items.statement: There are Weyl group elements s_i ∈ J_i, defined in [36, §5.6] (cf. [51, §6.2], where in most cases they are s_1^ϖ, s_1, with an added complication when n = 1 and G is special orthogonal); both s_1, s_2 exchange (up to scalars) e_{N+j}^+ and e_{N+j}^− for 1 ⩽ j ⩽ n and preserve V ⊆ V_n. T_i is supported on Js_iJ.
items.note: Cited input [36, §5.6]; generators of the affine Weyl group D_∞ of the Hecke algebra.

items.name: The cover (J°, λ°) of (J_ρ × J_π°, λ_ρ ⊗ λ_π°)
items.statement: The existence proof of the cover (J, λ) of (J_ρ × J_π, λ_ρ ⊗ λ_π) in [36] goes via first constructing a cover (J°, λ°) of (J_ρ × J_π°, λ_ρ ⊗ λ_π°); ℋ(G_n, λ°) and ℋ(G_n, λ) are not in general isomorphic but are closely related as in the next items.
items.note: Cited input [36]. Printed with a stray comma '(λ_ρ⊗, λ_π)' (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E9).

items.name: Case (i): f_i = 0
items.statement: ℋ(G_n, λ) is generated by T_1, T_2 with T_i supported on Js_iJ and (T_i − q^{f_i})(T_i + 1) = 0. (i) If n = 1 and either 𝒢^{(i)+}_{N_i} is the trivial orthogonal group (the orthogonal group on a zero space) or τ_π^(i) is not normalized by 𝒢^{(i)+}_{N_i}, then f_i = 0, i.e. T_i² = 1. Under the standing assumption of reducibility this happens for at most one i, and never if G is symplectic or unramified unitary.
items.note: Cited input [36, §6.3], specialized to depth zero (the character χ of loc. cit. is trivial).

items.name: Case (ii): T_i° ∈ ℋ(G_n, λ°) with the same parameter
items.statement: (ii) Otherwise, there is a corresponding element T_i° ∈ ℋ(G_n, λ°) with support J°s_iJ° satisfying the same quadratic relation as T_i, with the same parameter f_i.
items.note: Cited input [36, §6.3].

items.name: Inflation: finite Hecke algebra ↪ ℋ(G_n, λ°)
items.statement: By inflation there is a support-preserving algebra injection ℋ(𝒢_i°, τ_ρ ⊗ τ_π°) ↪ ℋ(G_n, λ°), and T_i° is in its image. Moreover ℋ(𝒢_i°, τ_ρ ⊗ τ_π°) ≃ ℋ(U((N_i+n)H̄ ⊕ V̄^an_(i))°, τ_ρ ⊗ τ_π^(i)).
items.note: Here ℋ(𝒢_i°, τ_ρ ⊗ τ_π°) is the endomorphism (Hecke) algebra of the representation of 𝒢_i° parabolically (Harish-Chandra) induced from the Levi GL_n(k_F) × 𝒢°_{N_1,N_2}. Harish-Chandra induction for finite reductive groups: no atlas stage.

items.name: Finite Hecke algebra is 2-dimensional; q^{f_i} as a dimension ratio
items.statement: (Lusztig [35, Theorem 8.6], at least when the ambient finite classical group has connected centre) ℋ(U((N_i+n)H̄ ⊕ V̄^an_(i))°, τ_ρ ⊗ τ_π^(i)) is two-dimensional, generated by an element satisfying the same quadratic relation (T − q^{f_i})(T + 1) = 0, with q^{f_i} the quotient of the dimensions of the two irreducible factors of the representation parabolically induced from τ_ρ ⊗ τ_π^(i). This can be computed using Lusztig's Jordan decomposition of characters (§7).
items.note: Cited input (Lusztig, Characters of reductive groups over a finite field, 1984; Howlett–Lehrer theory). The connected-centre caveat is why §7 must embed into a connected-centre group. No atlas stage.

items.name: Reduction of s_π to finite-group dimension ratios
items.statement: Combining §5 and §6: for depth-zero ρ ∈ 𝒜^σ_[0](F) (n = n_ρ) and π ∈ 𝒜_[0](G) in the dihedral case, {s_π(ρ), s_π(ρ′)} = {|f_1 ± f_2|/2n}, where f_i = 0 in case (i) and otherwise q^{f_i} is the ratio of the dimensions of the two irreducible constituents of the Harish-Chandra induction of τ_ρ ⊗ τ_π^(i) to U((N_i+n)H̄ ⊕ V̄^an_(i))°.
items.note: The section's upshot (the paper states that all of §6 is proved in [36, §6.3] and only explicated here); input to §7–8.

items.name: F_q/F_{q∘}-self-dual polynomial (§7.1)
items.statement: Fix F_q a finite field of odd cardinality q and F_{q∘} ⊆ F_q a subfield of index at most 2; σ generates Gal(F_q/F_{q∘}) and acts on F_q[X] coefficientwise. For P ∈ F_q[X] put P^σ(X) := σ(P(0))^{−1} X^{deg(P)} σ(P)(1/X). A monic P ∈ F_q[X] is F_q/F_{q∘}-self-dual if P = P^σ. When F_q = F_{q∘} one says simply self-dual (elsewhere: reciprocal).
items.note: Used to parametrize cuspidal representations of finite classical and unitary groups via characteristic polynomials of semisimple elements of the dual group ((7.2), §7.6, §7.7). Mathlib has Polynomial.reverse / Polynomial.mirror (Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/Mirror.lean:39) as ingredients but no σ-self-dual predicate. The statement needs P(0) ≠ 0 implicitly for P^σ to be defined.

items.name: Root characterization of self-duality (§7.1)
items.statement: A monic P ∈ F_q[X] is F_q/F_{q∘}-self-dual if and only if: (i) when F_q = F_{q∘}, for each root ζ of P (in some algebraic closure of F_q), ζ^{−1} is also a root of P, with the same multiplicity; (ii) when F_q ≠ F_{q∘}, for each root ζ of P, ζ^{−q∘} is also a root of P, with the same multiplicity.
items.note: Stated without proof. The printed criterion omits the multiplicities and is false for repeated roots (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E38); only irreducible P are used. Not in any library; no atlas stage.

items.name: Degrees of irreducible self-dual polynomials (§7.1)
items.statement: Let P be an irreducible F_q/F_{q∘}-self-dual monic polynomial. (i) When F_q = F_{q∘}, either P(X) = X ± 1 or deg(P) is even. (ii) When F_q ≠ F_{q∘}, deg(P) is odd.
items.note: Stated without proof. Underlies the split into the cases Q = X ± 1 and n_Q even in the table of §7.6, and n_Q odd in §7.7; it also forces a self-dual cuspidal τ₁ of GL_n to have n = 1 or n even (implicitly used on p. 19). Not in any library; no atlas stage.

items.name: Groups of classical type with connected centre (§7.2)
items.statement: 𝒢 is a connected reductive group over a finite field F_q of odd characteristic p, with connected centre and standard Frobenius ℱ, of one of the types: (i) SO_{2N+1}; (ii) GSp_{2N}; (iii) GSO⁺_{2N} or GSO⁻_{2N}, of Witt index N, N−1 respectively (GSO^±_{2N} the connected component of the full orthogonal similitude group GO^±_{2N}), excluding GSO⁺₂. The dual group 𝒢* (with dual Frobenius ℱ) acts naturally on an F̄_q-vector space 𝒱 with F_q-structure and form, of dimension 2N, 2N+1, 2N respectively. In case (iii) 𝒱 has type +1 if it has Witt index N and type −1 otherwise; the zero space has type +1.
items.note: Section 7 uses notation independent of the rest of the paper. These are the connected-centre groups into which the classical groups of §7.3 embed. Nothing on finite reductive groups, Deligne–Lusztig induction or Lusztig series exists in Mathlib or TauCeti (declarations index and sources grepped for Lusztig/HarishChandra/cuspidal), and no atlas stage plans them (all atlas roadmaps grepped for Deligne–Lusztig, Lusztig, finite reductive, Lie type, Harish-Chandra, cuspidal unipotent; only unrelated hits such as CharacterTheory Layer 9 'the representation theory of GL₂(𝔽_q)').

items.name: Partition into geometric Lusztig series ([32, §7.6])
items.statement: Let ℰ(𝒢^ℱ) be the set of equivalence classes of irreducible complex representations of 𝒢^ℱ (𝒢 with connected centre). Then ℰ(𝒢^ℱ) = ⋃_s ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s), s running over conjugacy classes of semisimple elements of 𝒢^{*,ℱ} (rational and geometric classes coincide since Z(𝒢) is connected), where π ∈ ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s) if and only if there is an ℱ-stable maximal torus 𝒯 of 𝒢* containing s with ⟨π, R^𝒢_𝒯 s⟩ ≠ 0 (R^𝒢_𝒯 s the Deligne–Lusztig representation, ⟨·,·⟩ the invariant inner product on class functions).
items.note: Cited input (Lusztig, Invent. Math. 1977, §7.6; the paper refers to Cabanes–Enguehard [13] / Digne–Michel [15] for definitions). Nothing on finite reductive groups, Deligne–Lusztig induction or Lusztig series exists in Mathlib or TauCeti (declarations index and sources grepped for Lusztig/HarishChandra/cuspidal), and no atlas stage plans them (all atlas roadmaps grepped for Deligne–Lusztig, Lusztig, finite reductive, Lie type, Harish-Chandra, cuspidal unipotent; only unrelated hits such as CharacterTheory Layer 9 'the representation theory of GL₂(𝔽_q)').

items.name: Jordan decomposition of characters: bijection and (7.1) ([32, Cor. 7.10], [13, Thm 15.8])
items.statement: For 𝒢 with connected centre and s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} semisimple, the centralizer 𝒢*_s is a connected reductive group of the same rank as 𝒢, and there is a bijection ψ^𝒢_s : ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s) → ℰ(𝒢^{*,ℱ}_s, 1) such that for every π ∈ ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s) and every ℱ-stable maximal torus 𝒯 containing s, (7.1) ε_𝒢 ⟨π, R^𝒢_𝒯 s⟩ = ε_{𝒢_s} ⟨ψ^𝒢_s(π), R^{𝒢*_s}_𝒯 1⟩, where ε_𝒢 = (−1)^{F_q-rank(𝒢)} ([15, Definition 8.3]).
items.note: Cited input (Lusztig 1977 Cor. 7.10 and §7.8; Cabanes–Enguehard Thm 15.8). The paper remarks that everything in this subsection extends to disconnected centre with rational Lusztig series in place of geometric ones. This is the central tool of §7: it reduces the parameter computation to unipotent representations of centralizers. Nothing on finite reductive groups, Deligne–Lusztig induction or Lusztig series exists in Mathlib or TauCeti (declarations index and sources grepped for Lusztig/HarishChandra/cuspidal), and no atlas stage plans them (all atlas roadmaps grepped for Deligne–Lusztig, Lusztig, finite reductive, Lie type, Harish-Chandra, cuspidal unipotent; only unrelated hits such as CharacterTheory Layer 9 'the representation theory of GL₂(𝔽_q)').

items.name: Jordan decomposition: uniform degree ratio
items.statement: In the setting of the Jordan decomposition ψ^𝒢_s, there is a uniform constant c_s with dim π = c_s dim ψ^𝒢_s(π) for all π ∈ ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s); explicitly, writing d_{p′} for the maximal divisor of d coprime to p, c_s = |𝒢^{*,ℱ}|_{p′} |𝒢^{*,ℱ}_s|^{−1}_{p′}.
items.note: Cited input ([32, §7.8]). Used so that the quotient dim(π₁)/dim(π₂) (hence q^{f_τ}) is the same on both sides of the Jordan decomposition. Nothing on finite reductive groups, Deligne–Lusztig induction or Lusztig series exists in Mathlib or TauCeti (declarations index and sources grepped for Lusztig/HarishChandra/cuspidal), and no atlas stage plans them (all atlas roadmaps grepped for Deligne–Lusztig, Lusztig, finite reductive, Lie type, Harish-Chandra, cuspidal unipotent; only unrelated hits such as CharacterTheory Layer 9 'the representation theory of GL₂(𝔽_q)').

items.name: Jordan decomposition and cuspidality
items.statement: If the identity components of the centres of 𝒢* and 𝒢*_s have the same F_q-rank, then π ∈ ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s) is cuspidal if and only if ψ^𝒢_s(π) is cuspidal; otherwise no representation in ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s) is cuspidal.
items.note: Cited input ([32, §7.8]). Gives the classification of cuspidals of 𝒢^ℱ by pairs (s, τ) with τ cuspidal unipotent of 𝒢^{*,ℱ}_s. Nothing on finite reductive groups, Deligne–Lusztig induction or Lusztig series exists in Mathlib or TauCeti (declarations index and sources grepped for Lusztig/HarishChandra/cuspidal), and no atlas stage plans them (all atlas roadmaps grepped for Deligne–Lusztig, Lusztig, finite reductive, Lie type, Harish-Chandra, cuspidal unipotent; only unrelated hits such as CharacterTheory Layer 9 'the representation theory of GL₂(𝔽_q)').

items.name: Lusztig's classification of cuspidal unipotent representations of classical groups
items.statement: Lusztig classified the irreducible cuspidal unipotent representations of classical groups; in particular there is at most one irreducible cuspidal unipotent representation for each such group (existence conditions as encoded in (7.2): Sp_{2n} and SO_{2n+1} need n = m² + m; SO^±_{2n} needs n = m² with type (−1)^m; U_a needs a = (m² + m)/2).
items.note: Cited input ([32, p. 172]; Lusztig 1977). The uniqueness is used again in the proof of Proposition 7.9 ('these Lusztig series contain only one cuspidal representation each'). The parenthetical existence conditions are read off from (7.2) and §7.7, not stated separately in the paper. items.name: (7.2)(i): cuspidal representations of SO_{2N+1}(F_q)
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be as in §7.2. For s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} semisimple let P_s ∈ F_q[X] be its characteristic polynomial on 𝒱, 𝒱₊ its (+1)-eigenspace and 𝒱₋ its (−1)-eigenspace. There is a bijection between the equivalence classes of irreducible cuspidal representations of 𝒢^ℱ and the conjugacy classes of semisimple s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} such that P_s(X) = ∏_P P(X)^{a_P} (product over irreducible self-dual monic P over F_q) with: Σ_P a_P deg(P) = dim 𝒱; for P(X) ≠ (X ± 1), a_P = ½(m_P² + m_P) for some integer m_P ≥ 0; and, writing a₊ := a_{(X−1)}, a₋ := a_{(X+1)}, there are integers m₊, m₋ ≥ 0 such that (i) if 𝒢 = SO_{2N+1} then a₊ = 2(m₊² + m₊) and a₋ = 2(m₋² + m₋).
items.note: Derived in the paper from Jordan decomposition plus Lusztig's classification ([32, p. 172]). The integers m_P, m_± are the inputs to the parameter table of §7.6. items.name: (7.2)(ii): cuspidal representations of GSp_{2N}(F_q)
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be as in §7.2. For s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} semisimple let P_s ∈ F_q[X] be its characteristic polynomial on 𝒱, 𝒱₊ its (+1)-eigenspace and 𝒱₋ its (−1)-eigenspace. There is a bijection between the equivalence classes of irreducible cuspidal representations of 𝒢^ℱ and the conjugacy classes of semisimple s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} such that P_s(X) = ∏_P P(X)^{a_P} (product over irreducible self-dual monic P over F_q) with: Σ_P a_P deg(P) = dim 𝒱; for P(X) ≠ (X ± 1), a_P = ½(m_P² + m_P) for some integer m_P ≥ 0; and, writing a₊ := a_{(X−1)}, a₋ := a_{(X+1)}, there are integers m₊, m₋ ≥ 0 such that (ii) if 𝒢 = GSp_{2N} then a₊ = 2(m₊² + m₊) + 1 and a₋ = 2m₋², where 𝒱₋ is an even-dimensional orthogonal space of type (−1)^{m₋}.

items.name: (7.2)(iii): cuspidal representations of GSO^±_{2N}(F_q)
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be as in §7.2. For s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} semisimple let P_s ∈ F_q[X] be its characteristic polynomial on 𝒱, 𝒱₊ its (+1)-eigenspace and 𝒱₋ its (−1)-eigenspace. There is a bijection between the equivalence classes of irreducible cuspidal representations of 𝒢^ℱ and the conjugacy classes of semisimple s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} such that P_s(X) = ∏_P P(X)^{a_P} (product over irreducible self-dual monic P over F_q) with: Σ_P a_P deg(P) = dim 𝒱; for P(X) ≠ (X ± 1), a_P = ½(m_P² + m_P) for some integer m_P ≥ 0; and, writing a₊ := a_{(X−1)}, a₋ := a_{(X+1)}, there are integers m₊, m₋ ≥ 0 such that (iii) if 𝒢 = GSO^±_{2N} then a₊ = 2m₊² and a₋ = 2m₋², where 𝒱_± is an even-dimensional orthogonal space of type (−1)^{m_±}.

items.name: Jordan decomposition commutes with Harish-Chandra induction (Shoji)
items.statement: Let s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} be semisimple and ℒ* ⊆ 𝒫* an ℱ-stable Levi subgroup of an ℱ-stable parabolic of 𝒢* with s ∈ ℒ*, with corresponding ℱ-stable ℒ ⊆ 𝒫 in 𝒢. Then ℒ*_s is an ℱ-stable (not necessarily proper) Levi subgroup of 𝒢*_s contained in an ℱ-stable parabolic 𝒫*_s, and the square ψ^𝒢_s ∘ Ind^𝒢_{ℒ,𝒫} = Ind^{𝒢*_s}_{ℒ*_s,𝒫*_s} ∘ ψ^ℒ_s : ℰ(ℒ^ℱ, s) → 𝐙ℰ(𝒢^{*,ℱ}_s, 1) commutes (vertical maps Harish-Chandra induction, extended to virtual characters 𝐙ℰ).
items.note: Cited input: a result of Shoji, 'extracted from the appendix to [16]' (Fong–Srinivasan 1989). The paper only needs the two special cases below. items.name: Case 𝒢*_s ⊆ ℒ*: induction preserves irreducibility
items.statement: In the setting above, if 𝒢*_s ⊆ ℒ* then Ind^𝒢_{ℒ,𝒫} and Ind^{𝒢*_s}_{ℒ*_s,𝒫*_s} preserve irreducibility and the Jordan-decomposition square commutes by (7.1). The same holds when 𝒫 is not ℱ-stable, replacing Ind^𝒢_{ℒ,𝒫} by the Deligne–Lusztig map ε_𝒢 ε_ℒ R^𝒢_{ℒ⊂𝒫}; then the square commutes by definition of ψ^𝒢_s.

Consequence: when 𝒢*_s ⊆ ℒ* the induced representation is irreducible, so reducibility (the case of interest) requires 𝒢*_s ⊄ ℒ* — (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E16). items.name: Maximal Levi: reducibility and the quadratic relation (connected centre)
items.statement: Suppose ℒ is a maximal proper Levi subgroup and τ ∈ ℰ(ℒ, s) is cuspidal. Then 𝒩_𝒢(ℒ)/ℒ has order 1 or 2, and Ind^𝒢_ℒ τ is reducible if and only if 𝒩_𝒢(ℒ)/ℒ has order 2 and a representative w of the nontrivial coset normalizes τ. In that case Ind^𝒢_{ℒ,𝒫} τ = π₁ ⊕ π₂ with dim(π₁) > dim(π₂) (strict by [35, Theorem 8.6]), and End_{𝒢^ℱ}(Ind^𝒢_{ℒ,𝒫} τ) is two-dimensional with a quadratic generator T satisfying (T + 1)(T − q^{f_τ}) = 0, q^{f_τ} = dim(π₁)/dim(π₂).
items.note: Cited input: Howlett–Lehrer/Lusztig theory of Hecke algebras of Harish-Chandra induction as in Lusztig's book [35, §8, Theorem 8.6]. items.name: Finite classical groups with disconnected centre and their similitude groups (§7.3)
items.statement: 𝒢 is a classical group over F_q (p odd) with standard Frobenius ℱ: (i) SO_{2N+1}; (ii) Sp_{2N}; (iii) SO⁺_{2N} or SO⁻_{2N}, of Witt index N, N−1, excluding SO⁺₂. In cases (ii), (iii) 𝒢 is embedded in a group 𝒢̃ with connected centre of the type in §7.2 (GSp_{2N}, GSO^±_{2N}); the dual map 𝒢̃* → 𝒢* sends conjugacy classes of semisimple elements of 𝒢̃^{*,ℱ} to (rational) 𝒢^{*,ℱ}-conjugacy classes of semisimple elements of 𝒢^{*,ℱ}.
items.note: Case (i) has connected centre and was handled in §7.2. Similitude groups GSp/GSO over finite fields are not in Mathlib/TauCeti (only symplecticGroup and orthogonal matrix groups). items.name: Splitting of geometric conjugacy classes
items.statement: For 𝒢 as in §7.3(ii),(iii), the geometric conjugacy class of a semisimple s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} splits into two 𝒢^{*,ℱ}-conjugacy classes if and only if 𝒢*_s is disconnected, which happens if and only if both 1 and −1 are eigenvalues of s.
items.note: Stated without proof (standard). For Sp_{2N} (dual SO_{2N+1}) 1 is always an eigenvalue, so the condition is that −1 is an eigenvalue. items.name: Rational Lusztig series and restriction from 𝒢̃ ([13, Prop. 15.6])
items.statement: ℰ(𝒢^ℱ) = ⋃_s ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s), s running over 𝒢^{*,ℱ}-conjugacy classes of semisimple elements of 𝒢^{*,ℱ} (rational Lusztig series); each geometric series is the union of at most two rational series. If s̃ ∈ 𝒢̃^{*,ℱ} maps to s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ}, then ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s) is exactly the set of irreducible components of the restrictions to 𝒢^ℱ of the representations in ℰ(𝒢̃^ℱ, s̃).
items.note: Cited input: Cabanes–Enguehard [13, Proposition 15.6]. items.name: Cuspidals of 𝒢^ℱ are constituents of restricted cuspidals of 𝒢̃^ℱ
items.statement: An irreducible representation of 𝒢^ℱ is cuspidal if and only if it is a component of the restriction of an irreducible cuspidal representation of 𝒢̃^ℱ. An irreducible cuspidal representation of 𝒢̃^ℱ restricts to 𝒢^ℱ as a sum of at most two pieces, inequivalent but of the same dimension when there are two (being 𝒢̃^ℱ-conjugate).
items.note: Stated without proof; follows from Clifford theory since 𝒵(𝒢̃^ℱ)𝒢^ℱ has index 2 in 𝒢̃^ℱ. TauCeti has Clifford's theorem in general form (FDRep.clifford_restrict_iso, TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Induction/Clifford/Equivalence.lean:281) but not this specialization; the finite-group-of-Lie-type content (cuspidality) is absent everywhere.

items.name: Restriction of cuspidals in quadratic-unipotent series ([32, Lemma 8.9])
items.statement: Let s̃ ∈ 𝒢̃^{*,ℱ} be such that its image s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} is an involution and ℰ(𝒢̃^ℱ, s̃) contains an irreducible cuspidal representation π. Then π|_{𝒢^ℱ} is irreducible if and only if s = ±1. (s = −1 is not possible when 𝒢 = Sp_{2n}.)

items.name: Deligne–Lusztig induction is a bijection on series when the centralizer lies in the Levi ([13, Thm 8.27])
items.statement: Let ℒ be an ℱ-stable Levi subgroup of 𝒢 and 𝒫 a (not necessarily ℱ-stable) parabolic with Levi ℒ, and ℒ*, 𝒫* the corresponding subgroups of 𝒢*. If s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} is semisimple with 𝒢*^{∘}_s 𝒢^{*,ℱ}_s ⊆ ℒ* (𝒢*^{∘} the connected component), then ε_𝒢 ε_ℒ R^𝒢_{ℒ⊂𝒫} : ℰ(ℒ^ℱ, s) → ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s) is a bijection. Moreover (cf. [32, §7.9]) with c_{ℒ,𝒢} = |𝒢^ℱ|_{p′} |ℒ^ℱ|^{−1}_{p′}, dim(ε_𝒢 ε_ℒ R^𝒢_{ℒ⊂𝒫}(π)) = c_{ℒ,𝒢} dim(π) for π ∈ ℰ(ℒ^ℱ, s); and when the connected centres of 𝒢* and ℒ* have the same F_q-rank, π is cuspidal if and only if ε_𝒢 ε_ℒ R^𝒢_{ℒ⊂𝒫} π is cuspidal.

items.name: The minimal F-stable Levi ℒ* containing the centralizer of s
items.statement: Given s̃ ∈ 𝒢̃^{*,F} mapping to s ∈ 𝒢^{*,F} with ℰ(𝒢̃^F, s̃) containing a cuspidal, let ℒ* be the minimal F-stable Levi subgroup of 𝒢* containing the centralizer of s (a Levi of a parabolic subgroup that need not be F-stable). With V_0 = ker(s² − 1), ℒ* = 𝒢*_s whenever s|_{V_0} = ±1. The connected centres of ℒ* and 𝒢* have the same F_q-rank, so twisted Deligne–Lusztig induction ε_𝒢ε_ℒR^𝒢_{ℒ⊂𝒫} gives a bijection between the cuspidal representations in ℰ(ℒ^F, s) and in ℰ(𝒢^F, s), multiplying dimensions by c_{ℒ,𝒢} = |𝒢^F|_{p′}|ℒ^F|_{p′}^{−1}. The corresponding ℒ̃ is a product of general linear groups with twisted Frobenius and a single classical group 𝒢̃_0 with connected centre, whose dual acts on V_0, so the (ir)reducibility of the restriction to ℒ^F is that of its 𝒢̃_0-factor. ℒ* is not the stabilizer of the decomposition of V into rational primary components, which need not be a Levi subgroup (sourceIssue E40).

items.name: Lemma 7.3: extension to the similitude group
items.statement: Let π ∈ ℰ(𝒢^ℱ, s) be an irreducible cuspidal representation and let s̃ ∈ 𝒢̃^{*,ℱ} be a semisimple element mapping to s. The following are equivalent: (i) π extends to an irreducible representation in ℰ(𝒢̃^ℱ, s̃); (ii) the centralizer 𝒢*_s is connected; (iii) at most one of ±1 is an eigenvalue of s.

items.name: Lemma 7.4(i): same Hecke algebra when w normalizes τ̃
items.statement: Setting: s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} semisimple, ℒ* a maximal proper ℱ-stable Levi in an ℱ-stable parabolic 𝒫* of 𝒢* with s ∈ ℒ* (printed: 𝒢*_s ⊆ ℒ*, which would make the lemma vacuous; PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E16), ℒ, 𝒫 the corresponding subgroups of 𝒢, lifts s̃, ℒ̃*, 𝒫̃* and ℒ̃, 𝒫̃ ⊆ 𝒢̃; τ ∈ ℰ(ℒ^ℱ, s) cuspidal, occurring with multiplicity one in the restriction of a cuspidal τ̃ ∈ ℰ(ℒ̃^ℱ, s̃); w a representative of the nontrivial element of 𝒩_𝒢(ℒ)/ℒ. (i) If w normalizes τ̃, then w normalizes τ and End_𝒢(Ind^𝒢_{ℒ,𝒫} τ) ≃ End_{𝒢̃}(Ind^{𝒢̃}_{ℒ̃,𝒫̃} τ̃) as Hecke algebras (the quadratic relations (T+1)(T−q^{f_τ}) = 0 coincide).

items.statement: Res^{𝒢̃}_𝒢 Ind^{𝒢̃}_{ℒ̃,𝒫̃} τ̃ = ⊕_{γ ∈ ℒ̃/𝒩_{ℒ̃}(τ)} Ind^𝒢_{ℒ,𝒫} τ^γ = ⊕_{γ ∈ ℒ̃/𝒩_{ℒ̃}(τ)} ⊕_{i=1}^{ℓ} π_i^γ, where Ind^𝒢_{ℒ,𝒫} τ = ⊕_{i=1}^{ℓ} π_i with ℓ = 2 if w normalizes τ and ℓ = 1 otherwise.

items.name: The isomorphism ℒ̃^ℱ ≃ GL_n^ℱ × 𝒢̃₀^ℱ
items.statement: Write ℒ^ℱ ≃ GL_n^ℱ × 𝒢₀^ℱ with 𝒢₀ a (possibly trivial) classical group of the same family as 𝒢, τ = τ₁ ⊗ τ₀ with τ₁ a self-dual irreducible cuspidal representation of GL_n^ℱ, and 𝒢̃₀ the similitude group of 𝒢₀ (the multiplicative group if 𝒢₀ is trivial), with similitude map μ : 𝒢̃₀^ℱ → F_q^× (the identity if 𝒢₀ is trivial). With respect to a Witt basis e₋_N, …, e₋_1, e₊_1, …, e₊_N for which ℒ^ℱ is the standard stabilizer of ⟨e₋_N, …, e₋_{N−n+1}⟩ (e₋_1, e₊_1 spanning the anisotropic part in the non-split orthogonal case), the map (g, h) ↦ diag(g, h, μ(h) w_n (g^{−1})^T w_n^{−1}) (g ∈ GL_n^ℱ, h ∈ 𝒢̃₀^ℱ; w_n antidiagonal with entries 1) is an isomorphism GL_n^ℱ × 𝒢̃₀^ℱ → ℒ̃. items.name: Representative w and its action (7.6)
items.statement: Let ε be the sign such that 𝒢 preserves an ε-symmetric form. If 𝒢 is symplectic or n is even, take w(e_i^±) = e_i^± for 1 ≤ i ≤ N − n and w(e_i^−) = e_i^+ and w(e_i^+) = ε e_i^− for N − n < i ≤ N (the printed w(e_i^±) = ε e_i^∓ is not an isometry when ε = −1; sourceIssue E39). This w preserves the ε-symmetric form and has determinant (−ε)^n, so it lies in the symplectic group for ε = −1 and in the special orthogonal group for ε = 1 when n is even; it is block antidiagonal and its conjugation action on ℒ̃, transported to GL_n^ℱ × 𝒢̃₀^ℱ, is (7.6) (g, h) ↦ (μ(h)(g^{−1})^T, h). Since τ₁ is self-dual, (7.6) intertwines τ₁ ⊗ τ̃₀ with itself if the central character of τ₁ is trivial; the only case with non-trivial central character is τ₁ the quadratic character, where (7.6) intertwines τ₁ ⊗ τ̃₀ with itself if and only if τ̃₀ ≃ τ̃₀ ⊗ (τ₁ ∘ μ).

items.name: Representative w for even orthogonal groups with n = 1

items.name: Lemma 7.8: symplectic groups
items.statement: Let 𝒢 = Sp_{2N}, ℒ a maximal proper Levi with ℒ^ℱ ≃ GL_n^ℱ × 𝒢₀^ℱ (𝒢₀ a possibly trivial symplectic group), τ = τ₁ ⊗ τ₀ cuspidal in ℰ(ℒ^ℱ, s), normalized by w, τ₁ ∈ ℰ(GL_n^ℱ, s₁), τ₀ ∈ ℰ(𝒢₀^ℱ, s₀) (s₀ = 1 if 𝒢₀ is trivial, its dual being SO₁), and τ̃ a cuspidal in ℰ(ℒ̃^ℱ, s̃) whose restriction to ℒ contains τ. Then τ̃ is normalized by w unless τ₁ is the non-trivial quadratic character of GL₁^ℱ and −1 is not an eigenvalue of s₀.
items.note: Remark (p. 20): since 1 is always an eigenvalue of s₀ ∈ SO_{2N'+1}, '−1 not an eigenvalue of s₀' is equivalent to τ₀ extending to 𝒢̃₀^ℱ, by Lemma 7.3. Proof uses Lemma 7.7 and the index-two twist criterion. With Lemma 7.4 this gives the Sp rows of the §7.6 table (f_τ = 0 exactly when m₋ = 0 in the X + 1 row). items.name: Index-two twisting criterion (used in the proof of Lemma 7.8)
items.statement: Let τ̃₀ be an irreducible representation of 𝒢̃₀^ℱ = GSp^ℱ_{2(N−1)} and χ = τ₁ ∘ μ the non-trivial quadratic character of 𝒢̃₀^ℱ, trivial on the index-two subgroup 𝒵(𝒢̃₀^ℱ)𝒢₀^ℱ. Then τ̃₀ ⊗ χ ≃ τ̃₀ if and only if the restriction of τ̃₀ to 𝒵(𝒢̃₀^ℱ)𝒢₀^ℱ is reducible, i.e. τ̃₀ restricts reducibly to 𝒢₀^ℱ.
items.note: Standard Clifford theory for an index-two normal subgroup, used without proof (also in Corollary 7.10). TauCeti has general Clifford theory (FDRep.clifford_restrict_iso) and index-two induced-character lemmas (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Induction/IndexTwo.lean) but not this twist criterion; InductionRestriction Layer 5 ('Clifford theory over a normal subgroup') covers Clifford's theorem and the Clifford correspondence, not this corollary.

items.name: Proposition 7.9(i): extension of cuspidals of GSO^±_{2N} to GO^±_{2N}
items.statement: Let τ ∈ ℰ(SO^{±,ℱ}_{2N}, s) be an irreducible cuspidal representation and τ̃ ∈ ℰ(GSO^{±,ℱ}_{2N}, s̃) an irreducible cuspidal representation, s̃ a semisimple element mapping to s. Then τ̃ extends to a representation of GO^{±,ℱ}_{2N} if and only if 1 is an eigenvalue of s.
items.note: For s² = 1 this is [32, Lemma 8.9]. Proof: the dual of GSO^±_{2N} is the special Clifford group C⁰(𝒱); τ̃ ≃ τ̃^c iff s̃ is C⁰(𝒱)-conjugate to c̃^{−1}s̃c̃ (uniqueness of the cuspidal in the series) iff some element of C¹(𝒱) centralizes s̃ iff 1 is an eigenvalue of s. Identifies when the affine Hecke parameter is zero (§6) and feeds Corollary 7.10. items.name: Proposition 7.9(ii): extension of cuspidals of SO^±_{2N} to O^±_{2N}
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 7.9, τ extends to a representation of O^{±,ℱ}_{2N} if and only if at least one of ±1 is an eigenvalue of s.
items.note: For s² = 1 this is due to Waldspurger [53] (proof of Proposition 4.3). Proof: when at most one of ±1 is an eigenvalue the series has a unique cuspidal and the criterion is whether the O-centralizer of s leaves SO; when both are eigenvalues, embed in SO^±_{2(N+1)} with Levi GL₁ × SO^±_{2N} and use Lemma 7.7(ii) and Lemma 7.4(i). Determines which cuspidal representations of even special orthogonal groups are O-stable, as needed in §6. items.name: The dual of GSO^±_{2N} is the special Clifford group
items.statement: The dual group of GSO^±_{2N} is the special Clifford group C⁰(𝒱), with an exact sequence 1 → 𝐆_m → C⁰(𝒱) → SO(𝒱) → 1, exact on points by Hilbert's Theorem 90. C⁰(𝒱) is the identity component, of index two, of the Clifford group C(𝒱) ⊆ A(𝒱)^× (A = A⁰ ⊕ A¹ the Z/2Z-graded Clifford algebra), C(𝒱) = C⁰(𝒱) ⊔ C¹(𝒱) with C^i(𝒱) = C(𝒱) ∩ A^i, and C(𝒱) maps onto O(𝒱).
items.note: Recalled without proof. Mathlib has CliffordAlgebra with its Z/2 grading (evenOdd) and lipschitzGroup/pinGroup/spinGroup (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/SpinGroup.lean:62), but not the special Clifford group GSpin, the G_m-extension of SO, or its identification with the dual of GSO. SpinRepresentations Layer 2 plans Pin/Spin double covers, not this.

items.name: Centralizers of s̃ in the odd part of the Clifford group
items.statement: Let s̃ ∈ C⁰(𝒱) be semisimple with image s ∈ SO(𝒱). Some element of C¹(𝒱) centralizes s̃ if and only if 1 is an eigenvalue of s. (If 1 is an eigenvalue, an anisotropic 1-eigenvector v ∈ C¹(𝒱) commutes with s̃.)
items.note: Key step of Proposition 7.9(i). The printed argument for the converse (elements of A¹ commuting with s̃ square to 0) has a gap (PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20/E20). The conclusion is correct. items.name: Corollary 7.10: even special orthogonal groups
items.statement: Let 𝒢 = SO^±_{2N}, 𝒢̃ = GSO^±_{2N}, τ ∈ ℰ(ℒ^ℱ, s) cuspidal for a maximal proper Levi ℒ, normalized by w, τ̃ ∈ ℰ(ℒ̃^ℱ, s̃) cuspidal with restriction containing τ, ℒ^ℱ ≃ GL_n^ℱ × 𝒢₀^ℱ (𝒢₀ a possibly trivial special orthogonal group, s₀ having no eigenvalues if 𝒢₀ is trivial), τ = τ₁ ⊗ τ₀, τ₁ ∈ ℰ(GL_n^ℱ, s₁), τ₀ ∈ ℰ(𝒢₀^ℱ, s₀). Then τ̃ is normalized by w in all but the following cases: (i) τ₁ is the trivial character of GL₁^ℱ and 1 is not an eigenvalue of s₀; (ii) τ₁ is the quadratic character of GL₁^ℱ and −1 is not an eigenvalue of s₀. Among the exceptional cases 𝒢₀ is never trivial (else 𝒢 = SO⁺₂).
items.note: Proof: Lemma 7.7 plus Proposition 7.9 and a case analysis on which of ±1 are eigenvalues of s₀. With Lemma 7.4 gives the SO^±_{2N} rows of the §7.6 table (f_τ = 0 when m₊ = 0 resp. m₋ = 0). items.name: §7.6 table: n = 1, Q = X − 1
items.statement: Let τ ∈ ℰ(ℒ^ℱ, s) be an irreducible cuspidal representation, ℒ a maximal proper Levi subgroup of a finite classical group 𝒢 of type (i) SO_{2N+1}, (ii) Sp_{2N} or (iii) SO^±_{2N}, with τ normalized by 𝒩_𝒢(ℒ); ℒ^ℱ ≃ GL_n^ℱ × 𝒢₀^ℱ, τ = τ₁ ⊗ τ₀, τ₁ ∈ ℰ(GL_n^ℱ, s₁) self-dual cuspidal, τ₀ ∈ ℰ(𝒢₀^ℱ, s₀). Write P_{s₀}(X) = ∏_P P(X)^{a_P} (X − 1)^{a₊} (X + 1)^{a₋} (P over irreducible self-dual monic polynomials of even degree), with a_P, a_± related to m_P, m_± as in (7.2), and Q the characteristic polynomial of s₁ ∈ GL_n^{*,ℱ}. Then End_{𝒢^ℱ}(Ind τ) has quadratic relation (T + 1)(T − q^{f_τ}) = 0 with f_τ = 2m₊ + 1 in cases (i), (ii) and f_τ = 2m₊ in case (iii), when n = 1 and Q = X − 1 (τ₁ trivial).
items.note: Obtained from Lemmas 7.4, 7.8, Corollary 7.10 and Lusztig's tables [34] via the Jordan decomposition. The row entry 2m₊ = 0 in case (iii) when m₊ = 0 matches the exceptional case Corollary 7.10(i) (f_τ = 0 by Lemma 7.4(ii)). These f_τ are the finite-Hecke parameters feeding the reducibility points s_π(ρ) in §8. items.name: §7.6 table: n = 1, Q = X + 1

items.name: §7.6 table: Q irreducible self-dual of even degree
items.statement: Let τ ∈ ℰ(ℒ^ℱ, s) be an irreducible cuspidal representation, ℒ a maximal proper Levi subgroup of a finite classical group 𝒢 of type (i) SO_{2N+1}, (ii) Sp_{2N} or (iii) SO^±_{2N}, with τ normalized by 𝒩_𝒢(ℒ); ℒ^ℱ ≃ GL_n^ℱ × 𝒢₀^ℱ, τ = τ₁ ⊗ τ₀, τ₁ ∈ ℰ(GL_n^ℱ, s₁) self-dual cuspidal, τ₀ ∈ ℰ(𝒢₀^ℱ, s₀). items.name: Finite unitary groups (§7.7)
items.statement: Let q = q∘² be an even power of an odd prime p, 𝒢 = GL_n over F_{q∘} with the twisted Frobenius ℱ, so 𝒢^ℱ is a unitary group (a subgroup of GL_n(F_q)). 𝒢* = GL_n acts naturally on an n-dimensional space 𝒱 with an F_q/F_{q∘}-hermitian form; for s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} semisimple, P_s(X) ∈ F_q[X] is its characteristic polynomial on 𝒱.

items.name: Cuspidal representations of finite unitary groups ([32, §9])
items.statement: The equivalence classes of irreducible cuspidal representations of the finite unitary group 𝒢^ℱ are in bijection with the conjugacy classes of semisimple s ∈ 𝒢^{*,ℱ} with P_s(X) = ∏_P P(X)^{a_P}, product over irreducible F_q/F_{q∘}-self-dual monic P ∈ F_q[X], and a_P = ½(m_P² + m_P) for some integer m_P ≥ 0.
items.note: Cited input: Lusztig 1977, §9. items.name: Unitary groups: reducibility and quadratic relation
items.statement: Let ℒ be a maximal proper ℱ-stable Levi subgroup of 𝒢 in an ℱ-stable parabolic 𝒫, ℒ^ℱ ≃ GL_m(F_q) × 𝒢₀^ℱ with 𝒢₀^ℱ unitary, and τ an irreducible cuspidal representation of ℒ^ℱ normalized by any representative w of the nontrivial element of 𝒩_𝒢(ℒ)/ℒ; so τ = τ₁ ⊗ τ₀ with τ₁ a conjugate-self-dual cuspidal representation of GL_m(F_q) and τ₀ cuspidal on 𝒢₀^ℱ. Then Ind^𝒢_{ℒ,𝒫} τ = π₁ ⊕ π₂ with dim(π₁) > dim(π₂), and End_{𝒢^ℱ}(Ind^𝒢_{ℒ,𝒫} τ) is two-dimensional with quadratic generator T satisfying (T + 1)(T − q^{f_τ}) = 0, q^{f_τ} = dim(π₁)/dim(π₂) > 1.
items.note: Unitary groups have connected centre, so no similitude comparison is needed. items.name: Unitary groups: the parameter f_τ
items.statement: In the unitary setting, let s₀ ∈ 𝒢₀^{*,ℱ} be semisimple with τ₀ ∈ ℰ(𝒢₀^ℱ, s₀), P_{s₀}(X) = ∏_P P(X)^{a_P} with a_P = ½(m_P² + m_P), and Q the irreducible characteristic polynomial of s₁ ∈ GL_m^{*,ℱ} with τ₁ ∈ ℰ(GL_m^ℱ, s₁), an irreducible F_q/F_{q∘}-self-dual monic polynomial of odd degree n_Q = m. Then f_τ = (2m_Q + 1) n_Q/2.
